documents.shelfmark: AGR Brussels, SEG 2559 (DECODE R992, R996, R997, R998)

system.summary: Syllabic nomenclator with homophones: numbers for letters and CV syllables, disguised letter-pair syllables, word codes, nulls.

diacritics.note: A '+' mark distinguishes groups (3+, e 2+, struck d = que).

system.sibling_key: Eight Brussels keys of 1647-98 (R958-R965) checked; none fits.
system.notes: About 3% of groups unassigned, mostly rare 3-digit name codes.

solution.what: Tried eight Brussels keys from the same series.
Two agents transcribed every cipher line and margin line from the images.
Anchors from n-grams repeated across letters, checked against the margin text.
Hard-EM monotone aligner of tokens to margin plaintext, seeded by the anchors; converged in two rounds.
Key applied to the four letters with no margin.
Key reproduces the ten margins; Ghent's fall (9 Mar 1678) appears in R998.

Statistical validation (docs/_validate.py): 7907 tokens, 180 types, es-golden-age order 4: reading -2.193 per letter; random keys -3.761 (z 8.9); key annealed onto shuffled ciphertext best -2.601 (mean -2.619, z 36.2); annealer on the real text -2.522. Verdict: pass.

Full texts listed in outcome.texts (George Lasry's request of 22 Oct 2026): linked tx/R985-R998.txt (cipher lines and margin text) and read/R985-R998.txt (key decryption, with the contemporary margin decipherment where there is one), one entry per letter, and key.json.

Reading audit (George Lasry's sentence test): read/R*.txt read through. The ten margined letters read from the contemporary margin decipherment; the key decryptions are syllable streams with groups not in the key, and the four letters without a margin (R992, R996-R998) have no text beyond that stream (docs/_check_reading.py: no sentences). Those four relabelled decoded, not read; class read -> read in part; method key recovered based on adjacent plaintext -> read from existing decipherment; fraction_read 0.97 -> 0.705 (5,489 of 7,784 tokens).

DECODE records R992, R996, R997, R998 re-fetched with the project cookie (b12_fetch.py): only the page images and DECODE's digit transcriptions; no decipherment attached, no margin on the cipher pages.

The key decodes of R992, R996-R998 printed token by token (b12_bal.py) and segmented into Spanish words by hand; second values found to hold across the letters: 63 = s (los, demás, sus), 77 = t (nosotros, atraer), the r-sign = stra/tra (nuestra, tratar), 69 = ru (prudencia); images checked at the breaks (R992 l. 10: 42, not 48 = 'resolución violenta').
_check_reading.py on the partial readings (bodies): R992 0.29, R996 0.40, R997 0.41, R998 0.13 clean sentences; all four stay decoded, not read.

Verification 5 (plain-bar rows): R985 and R991 were scored as whole files (key stream plus margin lines). Margin decipherments written out as read/R985_reading.md and read/R991_reading.md (R991's second unread margin word filled from the figures, 'de estos discursos'). Plain 0.333 and 0.417, explicit 1.0: the plain shortfall is names, period spellings and ordinary words missing from the es word list; both keep read on reader judgement.

validation.notes: claimed per-occurrence score -2.201; polyphony 0.0; 243 unread tokens left out; annealer on the real text from random keys reached -2.522

outcome.method_basis: The ten margined letters read from their contemporary margin decipherments. The syllabic nomenclator was rebuilt from those margins by a seeded EM aligner (key recovered based on adjacent plaintext) and decodes the four letters with no margin (R992, R996-R998), but only into syllable streams that do not yet build sentences.
outcome.notes: Four previously unread letters read in gist. 22 Oct 2026, reading audit: R992, R996-R998 (the four 'previously unread' letters) relabelled decoded, not read: key decryption is a syllable stream; the readings that stand are the ten contemporary margins. Class read -> read in part; method -> read from existing decipherment.

credits.note: marginal decipherments on 10 of the 14 letters, used to rebuild the key

reading_review.note: v5 check 23 Oct 2026 (1677, Spanish: plain share is a bar too): the sweep scored read/R985.txt whole, key syllable stream and line-broken margin text together (plain 0.571, explicit 1.0). The margin decipherment written out as running text, read/R985_reading.md (lines and split words joined, spelling kept): plain 0.333 (2/6), explicit 1.0 (6/6). The four sentences under the plain bar fail only on names (Amerong, Bremen), the period spellings the es word list lacks (alegrome, esperança, ay, ajuste, asemblea) and garantia/pretendida, which it also lacks; read as a reader both sentences hold with no hole, and the key decryption carries them group by group. Keeps read on reader judgement, the plain score being a word-list artefact here. texts.label: R992, 19 Sept 1677
texts.summary: Balbases at Nijmegen to Fuenmayor in Copenhagen, not deciphered before (gist from NOTES): On the protest the Imperial ministers published about the dissolution of the Bremen assembly. He has nothing to add: "de nuestra parte no nos queda que hacer sino es … temer" what the confederates will do.
texts.note: Re-read 22 Oct 2026 (b12): no contemporary decipherment, clear copy or edition exists (no margin; the DECODE record has only the images). The key decode was segmented into Spanish word by word, with second values that hold across the letters (63 = s, 77 = t, the r-sign = stra/tra, 69 = ru) and the images checked at the breaks; the partial reading read/R992_reading.md scores 0.29 clean sentences (5 of 17), below the 0.60 bar. Open: rare groups with no value in the key (no key material) and stretches where the homophones do not segment; the 1616-px greyscale scans do not settle the doubtful figures.
